issues.competing_evidence: Hoard+01 abstract reports candidate periods 0.1344 d and 0.2683 d and explicitly leaves the true orbital period ambiguous. Woudt & Warner+02 §2.7 favors the longer double-wave/ellipsoidal interpretation and gives 0.2689 +/-0.0007 d; Rawls et al. AAS abstract reports 0.2683 d.
issues.why_it_matters: The orbital period controls population placement and any period/evolution comparisons; the short and long aliases differ by a factor of two.
issues.needed_action: If adopting 6.4536 h as the preferred orbit, confirm that the double-wave interpretation is sufficient despite the inaccessible full Hoard+01 article; otherwise publish both candidate aliases without a canonical scalar.

issues.competing_evidence: Froning+12 and Hewitt+20 call CM Phe NL; Hewitt+20 §§2.11/4.3 says likely DN with missed outbursts because of faint absolute magnitude and sparse long-term light curve; Rawls et al. AAS abstract reports nine-year VY Scl-like luminosity changes possibly due to mass-transfer changes.
issues.why_it_matters: Subtype affects comparison of accretion state and radio limits among non-magnetic CVs. The evidence does not establish a unique subtype or evolutionary path.
issues.needed_action: Choose whether the online/catalog grouping should retain NL as historical discovery class with a “likely DN / VY Scl-like behavior” qualifier, or use a broader uncertain-CV subtype. Full Rawls dataset/paper would resolve the reported long-term behavior.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Methods describes 856 MHz bandwidth centered at 1.284 GHz (nominal 0.856-1.712 GHz); Ridder+23 Table 4 labels 0.43-2.1 GHz.
issues.why_it_matters: Bandpass labels affect comparison of spectral behavior and radio luminosity across catalog populations.
issues.needed_action: Use MeerKAT configured band 0.856-1.712 GHz for the observation row; check whether Ridder+23 intended a broader comparison interval or contains a table error before retaining its band as a system-level value.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 prints flux density <30 uJy and specific luminosity <4.6e15 erg s-1 Hz-1; the paper gives d=315.1 pc and Lnu=4πd²Fnu, which yields about 3.56e15. With preferred EDR3 d=308.39825 pc, the same flux limit yields 3.41e15.
issues.why_it_matters: Radio luminosity limits are used in population comparisons; a mismatch changes the limit by about 30% and may indicate an unstated flux threshold or a table calculation error.
issues.needed_action: Check Hewitt+20’s image RMS/peak map and exact unrounded 3-sigma limit or author-calculation convention; until then retain the published 4.6e15 and locally reproducible values as separate claims, without selecting one as verified.

issues.competing_evidence: Hoard+01 abstract and Hewitt+20 report M2-5 spectral type from TiO. Hewitt+20 §4.5 assumes M2=0.5 Msun (roughly M0) for an SED model because the model is insensitive to donor mass and invokes a possibly evolved donor.
issues.why_it_matters: The assumed mass is not a measured donor mass and is not straightforwardly matched to the M2-5 spectrum; component mass/evolution comparisons would be biased if the model input is used as a measurement.
issues.needed_action: Keep the 0.5 Msun value only as a model assumption unless the primary spectroscopy/dynamical source is recovered; verify whether the spectral type and model donor assumption can be reconciled by the evolved-donor interpretation.

issues.competing_evidence: Hoard+01 and Hoard & Wachter+98 full text were inaccessible (abstract/secondary reporting only); Hewitt+20 cites Jaidee & Lynga 1969 for the corrected historical identification but its original text was not retrieved. Exact SIMBAD/Gaia DR3 identifier membership independently secures the current counterpart.
issues.why_it_matters: Detailed photometric alias interpretation, original donor spectral classification, and historical identity correction have a weaker citation chain than the later measurements.
issues.needed_action: If community-facing text needs the original evidence, obtain Hoard+01/Hoard & Wachter+98/Jaidee & Lynga+69 full texts and verify the exact photometric/spectroscopic/identity chain. Current Gaia counterpart assignment does not depend on resolving the 1969 paper.

issues.competing_evidence: 2SXPS exact source products give 0.3-10 keV observed/unabsorbed power-law catalogue fluxes; Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1-10 and 0.1-10 keV converted unabsorbed comparison fluxes with a minimum 10% error floor. The soft-band value extrapolates below Swift/XRT 0.3 keV coverage; none is simultaneous with 2019 radio.
issues.why_it_matters: X-ray/radio comparisons are sensitive to bandpass, absorption correction, spectral assumptions, and epoch/state.
issues.needed_action: Before deriving an X-ray luminosity or comparing with radio, choose a uniform spectrum/band and epoch treatment or retain each as a separate model-dependent estimate; do not treat Table 4 values as native Evans fluxes.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 1 reports V=14.8-15.8 and M_V=7.3-8.3, but gives no explicit extinction correction/method in the table; numerical ranges resemble a distance-modulus transform using 315.1 pc.
